transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-12
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Jordan Patel (Redwood Solutions), Sara Lopez (Aquila Head of ML), Tom Nguyen (Aquila Platform), Priya Rao (Aquila SecOps), Miguel Alvarez (Aquila CTO)

Summary:
Quick sync on pilot metrics and sizing for Dedicated cluster. Reviewed current throughput, p95 latency spikes during morning batch jobs, discussed autoscaling policy tweaks and burst capacity for peak windows. Agreed on benchmark run and follow-up deliverables.

Topics:
- Current pilot results (latency, concurrency, cost)
- Autoscaling policy: scale-up/scale-down triggers, cooldown, burst tolerance
- Burst planning: short 5-30m peaks vs sustained load
- Security/network requirements for Dedicated (VPC, KMS, audit logs)
- Next steps and responsibilities

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: ok everyone thanks for joining, we're on for 45, quick roll call?
[00:05] Sara: hey this is Sara, um head of ML at Aquila.
[00:07] Tom: Tom here, platform.
[00:09] Priya: Priya SecOps.
[00:10] Miguel: Miguel CTO.
[00:12] Liam: Liam O'Connor from Redwood, se on the call.
[00:14] Jordan: Jordan as well.
[00:16] Maya: great, thanks. quick agenda, recap of the last week's run, go over the p95 spikes you saw on Tuesday morning, talk autoscale policies and burst sizing, and then action items.

[02:20] Sara: yeah so real quick numbers, our staging run last week averaged 120 rps during business hours, about 18k tokens per minute, p50 is fine at 120ms but p95 jumps to 1.8s when the batch ETL hits at 03:00 GMT. so we see that tail, cost is creeping up during those windows.

[03:05] Liam: ok that matches what we saw in the logs you uploaded, we flagged two things - the KV cache hit drops during the ETL batch because session tokens are long and batching flushes, and autoscaler is configured with conservative cooldowns so it doesn't pick up the fast ramp.

[04:10] Tom: can you remind us what the current Dedicated cluster size is?

[04:15] Jordan: right now you're on a 4xA100 profile with 8 GPUs reserved, we left headroom for a single burst node but the policy scales by 2 nodes every 5 minutes with a 10 minute cooldown, so short spikes don't scale fast enough.

[05:00] Priya: from a security side we need to understand whether burst nodes are in our VPC or if Redwood's shared pool is used, because we have to enforce KMS encryption and egress controls.

[05:30] Maya: important point, for Dedicated the burst nodes can be in the customer's VPC if they opt for private burst, otherwise we provide a Redwood-managed burst pool. Liam can confirm the default.

[06:05] Liam: yeah default is Redwood-managed for now, but we have the private burst option - it requires network peering and extra KMS config, adds a week to setup typically. We also have an option to pre-warm nodes during known windows.

[07:20] Sara: pre-warm sounds promising; our morning spikes are predictable around 03:00 GMT for model scoring after batch jobs. If pre-warm can bring nodes online in under two minutes that's ideal.

[08:05] Liam: pre-warm is usually 90-120s to reach ready state depending on image pull and kv cache warmup. The autoscaler can be configured to pre-provision N nodes at t-5 minutes. That plus an aggressive scale-up policy will handle the short spike.

[09:30] Tom: what's the cost delta if we pre-warm 2 nodes for 15 minutes every morning?

[09:40] Jordan: rough math - those two A100 nodes at reserved pricing come to about $X/day; for 15 minutes it's small relative to the sustained cost. we put an estimate in the spreadsheet, will send updated numbers after this call.

[10:50] Sara: on the performance front we also saw some tail due to long context windows in a subset of requests - ~6% of requests ask for 8k tokens. can we do prefix caching to reduce recompute?

[11:20] Liam: yes we can enable prefix/KV caching in the runtime; it reduces repeated prefix cost by about 30-60% depending on overlap. we just need to make sure the session ids are stable, otherwise cache miss rate will be high.

[12:40] Priya: for audit purposes we need to capture per-request metadata and store audit logs for 1 year, is that supported on Dedicated?

[12:55] Maya: yes Dedicated supports logs to customer S3 and can integrate with your SIEM, we need to document retention and format. Liam will share the template.

[14:00] Liam: i'll drop the audit log format and examples into the shared drive.

[15:15] Miguel: circling back to burst - how do you avoid noisy neighbor from a Redwood-managed pool? we can't have other tenants' workloads affecting our p95.

[15:35] Jordan: in Redwood-managed burst pools we use soft isolation with runtime QoS plus tenancy-aware scheduling. for strict isolation you'd want private burst or extra reserved capacity; we can simulate noisy neighbor in benchmarking.

[17:00] Sara: ok let's talk concrete autoscale knobs - what do you recommend for scale-up and scale-down thresholds?

[17:15] Liam: recommended starting point: scale-up when average GPU utilization > 60% for 30s OR queue depth > 10, scale by +2 nodes, max burst nodes = 6, scale-down after 300s cooldown and when utilization < 30% for 2 minutes. but for predictable short spikes, enable pre-warm N nodes at t-5m.

[18:50] Tom: the cooldown seems long - we worry about oscillation. can we use faster scale-down for small bursts?

[19:05] Liam: yes we can configure multiple policies: aggressive scale-down for nodes launched as part of a burst window (e.g., scale-down after 120s if queue is empty), and standard cooldown for sustained scale-up to avoid oscillation.

[20:30] Sara: will these policies be available via API so our infra can tune them?

[20:40] Maya: yes all policy configs are via the Redwood API and Console; Jordan will share sample API payloads.

[21:10] Sara: also, we want to cap cost per million tokens to a threshold, can we set budget alarms that trigger fallback to a smaller model or rate limit?

[21:30] Liam: yes we have routing policies: on cost threshold you can route to cheaper quantized variants or to hosted failover. Redwood Optimize can also recommend quantization profiles to hit your cost target.

[22:45] Priya: from compliance - SSO/SAML, RBAC scoping, and KMS key rotation - do you rotate keys automatically or do we manage rotation?

[23:05] Maya: Dedicated supports customer-managed keys (CMK) and auto-rotate is available. we'll include details in the security docs.

[24:20] Miguel: technical deep dive question - during the last run we saw a significant increase in cold-start latency after a redeploy. is that warm-up time related to KV warming or container start?

[24:45] Liam: it's a combo - container/driver init plus kv cache. container start can be 30-60s depending on image size, kv warmup another 60-90s, but with pre-warm and cache snapshots we can bring it down. we recommend snapshotting common prefix keys for faster warmups.

[26:10] Sara: for the benchmark we plan to simulate a 10x burst for 30 minutes to validate scaling and see cost impact - is that too aggressive?

[26:25] Jordan: sounds fine in a staging env; we recommend doing a stepped ramp: 1x, 3x, 6x, 10x for 10 minutes each, that will give us signal for scale-up velocity and any tail latencies.

[27:40] Tom: question: does Redwood support autoscaler metrics pushed to our Prometheus? we want to keep a single dashboard.

[27:55] Liam: yes we can stream metrics to your Prometheus push gateway; the Console also provides token-level breakdowns if you want.

[29:05] Sara: what's the expected end-state SLA if we go to Dedicated with private burst?

[29:20] Maya: with Dedicated + private burst and a committed capacity contract, we offer SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; we'll share the SLA doc.

[30:40] Priya: ok last security point: can you provide network diagram and peering instructions, plus a list of IP ranges for the Redwood-managed burst if we test that path?

[30:55] Maya: yes we'll include the network diagram, and if you test Redwood-managed burst we'll provide ephemeral IP ranges and a contact for emergency egress blocking.

[32:10] Miguel: rough timeline - if we get the sizing spreadsheet and do the 30-min burst next week, we'd like to decide on Dedicated commit by end of month. is that feasible?

[32:25] Maya: yes that's reasonable. final decision by end of October lines up with procurement.

[33:40] Jordan: i'll update the sizing sheet to include pre-warm costs and a couple of autoscale policy templates (aggressive, conservative).

[34:15] Sara: can you also include estimated cost per 1M tokens for the different model variants and for quantized vs full precision?

[34:30] Jordan: yep we'll add that table.

[35:05] Tom: quick clarification on burst billing - do you bill burst nodes at reserved rate or on-demand?

[35:20] Maya: burst nodes are billed at a short-term usage rate; if you opt for private burst and reserve capacity we can honor committed pricing for those nodes. we'll put options in the pricing attachment.

[36:45] Sara: any known limits on concurrent streams or websocket sessions? we have a real-time scoring path.

[36:55] Liam: default concurrent streams per GPU is 64, can be tuned via config; for real-time low-latency we recommend dedicated real-time lanes.

[38:10] Priya: we'll need the compliance pack and SOC2 cert for our procurement team - please send links.

[38:25] Maya: yes, sending now.

[39:10] Miguel: ok to recap, action items?

[39:20] Maya: recap: Liam updates autoscale and shares policy examples; Jordan updates sizing spreadsheet with pre-warm and cost breakdowns; Sara/Tom run the benchmark and collect logs; Maya to share security docs and pricing attachment. any other?

[40:05] Sara: that's it from us, thanks.

[40:10] Tom: thanks all.

[40:15] Liam: i'll follow up with the API payloads and log template.

[40:30] Maya: perfect, we'll reconvene after the benchmark, same time next week?

[40:38] Sara: same time works.

[40:40] Miguel: thanks, bye.

[40:45] Jordan: bye.

[41:00] End of recording.

Notes: transcription has occasional mis-hears (e.g., some product names), timestamps approximate.
